comments.content: The rented array is only returned on the success path. `EncodingUtil.SecureUtf8Encoding` is created with `throwOnInvalidBytes: true`, so `GetByteCount`/`GetBytes` throw `EncoderFallbackException` for a purpose containing an unpaired surrogate (purposes can come from untrusted input via `CreateProtector`), and `new byte[totalPurposeLen]` can throw as well. Any of those bypasses `ArrayPool<int>.Shared.Return`, so repeated failures silently drain the shared pool. Wrap the Rent/Return pair in try/finally.

comments.content: The hand-rolled `Measure7BitEncodedUIntLength`/`Write7BitEncodedInt` pair only produces identical bytes to the legacy `BinaryWriter.Write(string)` path if both agree exactly for every length. Existing tests (`KeyRingBasedDataProtectorTests.BuildAadFromPurposeStrings`) only use short purposes ("purpose", "purpose1", "yet another purpose"), so the multi-byte length-prefix path (purpose ≥ 128 UTF-8 bytes, and the 3/4/5-byte cases) is never exercised, and this NET10-only path is otherwise only reachable via an actual `Protect` call. Please add a test with a longer / multi-byte-UTF8 purpose (e.g. comparing against the `BinaryWriter`-built AAD) so a regression in the length encoding can't silently break unprotect across TFMs.

Now let me also double check the `Measure7BitEncodedUIntLength` matches `BinaryWriter.Write` for all lengths: BinaryWriter.Write(string) uses `7BitEncodedInt(byteCount)` where byteCount is the byte count and writes:
```
while (value >= 0x80) { _buffer[...] = (byte)(value | ~0x7F); value >>= 7; }
Buffer[0] = (byte)value;
```
Yes, identical to `Write7BitEncodedInt`.

Note BinaryWriter's loop condition is `value >= 0x80` (i.e., > 0x7F), same as `uValue > 0x7Fu`. Good.

Let me double check the `Measure7BitEncodedUIntLength` correctness at boundary 2^21 etc. Max 5 bytes for values up to uint.MaxValue; purpose lengths are int so ≤ 2^31-1 requiring 5 bytes: LZC(2^31-1)=1 → 31-1=30 → 30/7=4 → 5. And Write7BitEncodedInt for value 2^31-1: uValue=0x7FFFFFFF → iterations: writes bytes while >0x7F: 0x7FFFFFFF>0x7F → write, >>7 = 0x3FFFFF >0x7F → ... count: 4 iterations then final = 5 bytes. Match. Good.

For a 1-element array, `Rent(1)` will take from the shared per-core bucket — cheaper than GC allocation usually. Not material.
